statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: If someone was arrested or convicted under the name of a person whose identity was stolen or used without authorization, the aggrieved person may petition the chief judge of the circuit where the arrest occurred to correct the arrest or conviction and the official records by removing their name and substituting the offender's name if known. The committed route contract records the mechanism as a nunc pro tunc correction, removal and sealing mechanism with no elapsed waiting period: the verified petition may be filed upon learning of the record. It is not an ordinary conviction-expungement clock and is not routed through the ordinary expungement eligibility engine.
doNotImport: Do not route this matter through the ordinary Illinois expungement or sealing eligibility engine, waiting periods or exclusion lists; the route contract forbids it.
Do not substitute an ordinary expungement or sealing instrument, an official Illinois form or an invented form; no committed record names an official participant form for this route.
Do not treat a prostitution record on this route; the route contract records it as the separate branch of the same decision (IL:felony-prostitution-relief).
Do not invent a filing fee, a fee waiver, a service requirement, a copy count or a hearing rule; no committed record this family binds establishes any of them.
Do not decide that the record was in fact made in the participant's name by another person; that is the participant's verified allegation and the whole premise of the route.

requiredFacts.use: the person named in the caption of the petition
identity of the person named in the caption
mailing address, telephone and email of the petitioner
screening fact the route contract names; the record was made under the participant's name by another person
Item C1 of the petition: the identity-theft report and the mismatched identifiers, copied from the record itself
Item C2 of the petition: the Illinois judicial circuit where the arrest occurred, which fixes the chief judge petitioned
Item C3 of the petition, carried because the route contract records it as a required fact of the two-route decision; a prostitution record is a stop on this route
Item C4 of the petition: sentence completion, copied from the record
Item C5 of the petition: trafficking or victimization facts the route contract records as a required fact
Item C6 of the petition: whether Illinois automatic sealing has already reached the record, which the route contract records as a fact this route must collect

finalVerificationRequirements: Confirm that the record was made in the participant's name by another person; an ordinary arrest or conviction of the participant's own is a different Illinois route with a different instrument.
Fill Items C1 to C6 of the petition from the identity-theft report, the arrest record and the participant's own identity documents, never from memory.
Identify the Illinois judicial circuit where the arrest occurred; the petition goes to the chief judge of that circuit.
Ask the office of the chief judge of that circuit what it charges, how it accepts filings and who, if anyone, must be served before filing; no committed record establishes any of them.
Obtain the identity-theft report and the mismatched-identifier evidence the route contract names as packet components and file them with the petition.
The participant signs and dates the petition personally; the case number, if the court assigns one, is assigned at filing and never pre-filled.

filingDestination.statement: File the verified petition with the office of the chief judge of the Illinois judicial circuit where the arrest occurred, and ask that office what it charges and how it accepts filings before going. The compiled Illinois profile records that the aggrieved person may petition the chief judge of the circuit where the arrest occurred; the route-obligation census records the route's own destination field as not recorded, and the compiled profile answers it for this route.

postFilingTimeline.step: Read the filing-instructions page, fill Items C1 to C6 of the petition from the record itself, obtain the identity-theft report and the mismatched-identifier evidence, and sign and date the petition personally.

postFilingTimeline.step: File the petition and its attachments with the office of the chief judge of the Illinois judicial circuit where the arrest occurred, after asking that office what it charges, how it accepts filings and who must be served.
The chief judge may order the arrest or conviction and the official records corrected by removing the participant's name and substituting the offender's name if known.
